title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is seeing a mix of consolidation and funding as companies scramble to secure their positions in a rapidly evolving market. Meanwhile, the U.S. government continues to bolster its space resilience initiatives amid ongoing geopolitical tensions.

themes.title: M&A Activity Heats Up
themes.body: MDA Space's acquisition of Blue Canyon Technologies signals a strategic push into the U.S. market, highlighting the competitive landscape. This trend could lead to more consolidation as companies seek to enhance their capabilities.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy Continues
themes.body: ElevationSpace's $40 million Series B funding round adds to a growing list of capital raises in the sector, reflecting investor confidence. With True Anomaly also securing $190 million, the appetite for space ventures remains robust.

themes.title: Government Spending on Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup, which adds $1.4 billion to space resilience, underscores the U.S. commitment to maintaining its edge in space. This funding will likely support various initiatives, from satellite development to defense capabilities.

themes.title: Challenges in Orbital Operations
themes.body: Concerns about the durability of LEO hardware in the new orbital economy are becoming increasingly pressing. As NASA embarks on missions to study space weather, the implications for satellite longevity and performance could be significant.
